observation: The first plan and architecture rested on harness notes that were wrong in load-bearing ways (resume, hooks, sandbox binding). A full reset to refine with per-harness research against the real binaries (268 referenced claims) was needed before the design held. Notes about a harness are hypotheses; only a run against the binary is evidence.

The build was proven green three times before the manual run on the packaged desktop app, and the manual run found six defects between an agent asking and a human answering — including a plain-message fallback that made the ordinary review unanswerable and a review page that crashed on every real review. Every one was on a path no test drove end to end. The gate on this kind of package is the running app, not the lanes.

Two fixes were green in a test and dead on every real run: one asserted on a destroy spy that removes an already-removed tree (the real delete is fs.rm in the terminal transition), one read the return action off the event stream that production never uses (with the MCP bridge open it arrives via onToolCall). Both passed a sanity-break. A relocation must be proven per invocation mode, and a test must assert the observable effect (the directory on disk), not the seam it was written against.

An 'accepted gap' recorded as a weaker proof (files lost on resume) was in fact a broken loop (the resume hangs in a directory that no longer exists). A gap accepted without measuring its cost was accepted on a wrong premise; it had to be fixed inside the package after all.

Removing interception (5,452 lines) once the research showed every harness's interception fails open in a way that looks like success left a loop small enough to prove: the product change is ~540 net lines. Deleting the mechanism that must prove itself alive on every run beat hardening it.

The pipeline skills (review, retro, ship) were not invoked; their steps were done by hand and the item folder was never consolidated, so the PR carried 5,800 lines of research until ship ran. Run /ship; do not re-enact it.

Proving on the running app revealed the return gate (Stop hooks) exists only because the harness protocol discards the agent's final message, and that token/tool-call counts are collected from inside the session. Both are now separate packages (BA13, BA15). A proof run is also an audit of what it walks through.
